events.objective: Establish the real symptom onset and true blast radius. From logs and metrics around 11:45Z-13:59Z: (1) confirm whether customer-reported failures begin ~12:15Z; (2) determine which services actually show anomalies (error rate, latency, timeout, queue depth, retry counts, saturation) — explicitly including services upstream/downstream of payment-service; (3) characterize the error signature (status codes, exception types, timeout vs rejection vs silent drop) and check whether payment-service's success responses are masking failures (e.g. async settlement errors, queue backlog, webhook failures). Report whether payment-service error_rate is genuinely normal on ALL of its request paths.

Find what changed in the window 11:45Z-13:30Z across ALL services, not just payment-service: list deployments, config/feature-flag changes, credential/certificate or DNS changes, and dependency-graph facts — specifically what payment-service depends on and what shares those components (queue, DB, bank/acquirer connector, auth). Flag any change on a shared component that could break settlement while leaving payment-service's HTTP error rate green. Also search historical incidents for a prior occurrence of 'errors invisible on payment dashboard / transfer failures' to identify a precedent pattern.

Correlate the dependency/change findings with the true onset time and affected services identified by the observability task, to name the most likely faulting component and rule in/out the 'bank side or client app' hypothesis. Requires a's onset/blast-radius result and b's change list.

events.statement: Across all services, exactly one deployment occurred in the 2026-04-01→2026-04-02T13:59 window: dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0 at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z (author ci-bot, 'new CSV exporter'), status live, not rolled back.

Exactly one config change occurred: cfg-2502 on payment-service, key bank.api.timeout_ms, changed 3000 → 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, description 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'.
Both changes precede the 12:32Z report and the ~12:32 symptom window by over an hour (deploy 10:30, config 11:20); neither was rolled back.

payment-service's dependency edges are: payment-service → ledger-db (db), payment-service → bank-partner-api (external), payment-service → kafka (queue-produce); api-gateway → payment-service (http). ledger-db and kafka are marked shared=true; bank-partner-api is external and has_telemetry=false.

payment-service's only upstream caller is api-gateway; ledger-db's dependency query returns zero edges, so no additional downstream consumer chain of ledger-db is registered. No client-app/mobile component appears anywhere in payment-service's dependency graph.

Historical precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19) is titled 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' with the same symptom pair ('payment failures', 'bank api errors'), root cause 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)'; this is a lead only, not evidence about INC-005.

events.description: Do not have observability task's true onset time / affected-service blast radius (T1 output). Without it I cannot align the 10:30 deploy and 11:20 config change against the real onset, so 'most likely faulting component' is unanchored in time.
bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false; no metrics, logs or deployment data exist for it. No tool available to query partner-side status in this task.
ledger-db and kafka are shared=true (platform-owned) but no query was run against their available_metrics (turn budget exhausted), so their health at 12:00-13:00 is unchecked.

events.answer: The only changes in the incident window are a payment-service config change at 11:20 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000, "Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory") and a settlement-service deploy at 10:30 — both pre-date the ~12:32 report. payment-service depends directly on bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry) and on two SHARED platform components (ledger-db, kafka), and its only upstream is api-gateway. The "bank side or client app" hypothesis cannot be confirmed from change/dependency data: bank-partner-api has no telemetry, and no client-app component exists in payment-service's dependency graph. No faulting component can be named from these two data sources alone; the timeout config bump plus the direct external bank dependency make bank-partner-api the lead to test against the true onset.

events.statement: No deployments occurred in the reported-change window 11:45Z-13:30Z across all services (count=0).
No config/feature-flag changes occurred in 11:45Z-13:30Z across all services (count=0).

Widening to 08:00Z-14:00Z yields exactly one deployment: settlement-service v1.9.0 (dep-5510, 'Batch settlement report export', 'new CSV exporter') at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z, status live, not rolled back.

Widening config search to 08:00Z-14:00Z yields one change: payment-service key bank.api.timeout_ms changed 3000->5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory').

payment-service's dependency graph: -> ledger-db (db), -> bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry=false), -> kafka (queue-produce), and api-gateway -> payment-service (http). ledger-db and kafka are both marked shared=true.

Shared-component sharers: kafka is produced by order-service and payment-service, and consumed by settlement-service and notification-service; ledger-db is used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service. So settlement-service and payment-service both touch kafka and ledger-db.

Precedent leads from historical incidents (not current evidence): HIST-105 (2025-11-19) payment failures from bank-partner API 5xx, resolved by queued retries; HIST-106 (2025-06-30) 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' on settlement-service, symptoms 'tls handshake failures / expired certificate', resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert'; HIST-114 (2025-04-18) ledger-db disk full from retained WAL causing write failures.

Inference: the settlement-service deployment dep-5510 (10:30Z) and the shared kafka/ledger-db dependencies are the change candidates that could affect settlement while leaving payment-service's own HTTP error rate green; the 11:20Z timeout raise (3s->5s) would delay, not surface, bank-side errors on payment-service's panel.

Did not run metrics queries against kafka, ledger-db or settlement-service (task budget spent); has_telemetry=true for all three but no values were pulled.

events.answer: No deployment or config change occurred inside 11:45Z-13:30Z. The only changes nearby: a settlement-service deployment (dep-5510, v1.9.0, 10:30Z) on a service that shares both kafka and ledger-db with payment-service, and a payment-service config change (cfg-2502) at 11:20Z raising bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000. payment-service depends on ledger-db (shared with order/portfolio/settlement), kafka (shared with order/settlement/notification), and the external bank-partner-api; a change on settlement-service or the shared ledger-db/kafka path could break settlement while leaving payment-service's own HTTP error rate green.

events.statement: payment-service logged 311 ERROR events in 11:45–13:59Z; the dominant signatures are 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' (171x, first_seen 12:16:44Z) and 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140x, first_seen 12:15:27Z).

A cert-watcher WARN at 11:50:26Z predicted the exact failure onset: 'client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)'; the first mTLS rejection followed at 12:15:27Z, matching expiry to the second.

payment-service raw HTTP error_rate stayed flat across the whole window (min 0.1 / max 0.32%, unit '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)'), including every bucket from 12:15Z onward — the reported green dashboard is arithmetically real for that metric.

The same service's OTHER paths are not green: bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.2% to exactly 100.0 at the 12:15:00Z bucket and stays at 100.0 through 13:57Z, while payment_success_rate drops from ~99.3% (12:09Z) to 2.51% at 12:15Z and remains ~2-3% thereafter.

Request volume to payment-service did not change at onset: request_rate is ~100 req/s throughout (12:15Z avg 101.27, 13:57Z avg 99.55), so the failures are not a traffic surge — inbound requests keep being accepted while downstream settlement fails.

payment-service latency_p99 DROPS rather than rising at onset (323.5ms at 12:00Z → 140.0ms avg at 12:18Z bucket, staying ~135-145ms), consistent with failing fast on handshake rejection instead of hanging on the bank call — so the panel shows no latency anomaly either.

events.description: Could not query settlement-service logs (tool budget exhausted before execution) — whether async settlement/webhook paths emit their own errors or queue backlog is unverified.
Could not query notification-service logs (tool budget exhausted).
api-gateway logs for 12:00-13:59Z returned total_matched=0 over a data_range of 08:00-13:59Z — no gateway-side errors visible, but this could also mean the gateway does not log this failure mode.
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no logs/metrics; it can only be observed through payment-service ('we have no logs/metrics for it. Observe it through its callers').
Did not inspect queue-depth / retry-count / db_pool_in_use / saturation metrics for payment-service or its queue component.

events.answer: Customer-reported payment failures begin at ~12:15Z, not 12:15 but aligned exactly with the expiry of payment-service's mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z). payment-service's HTTP error_rate is genuinely flat (~0.2%) on the request path because calls to bank-partner-api fail asynchronously/are re-marked PENDING_RETRY rather than returning 5xx, but its own bank_api_error_rate jumps to 100% and payment_success_rate collapses 99%→~2.5% from the same 12:15Z bucket — so the "green" panel is blind, not normal.
